rules.title: Views and iterators for long chains
rules.what: Chain large transformations through .iterator or .view and materialise only the final result.
rules.why: Every map or filter on a strict collection allocates a new one: three links over a large collection are three full copies for one result.
rules.how: xs.view.map(f).filter(p).toVector; LazyList for streams; benchmark lazy against strict on the real volume.

patterns.note: Three chained strict transformations; candidate on large collections.

verify.how: Allocation or timing benchmark on representative volume for performance-motivated changes.

limits: On small collections the strict version is clearer and cheaper.

rules.title: Bounded parallelism, measured first
rules.what: Stay sequential by default; parallelise (.par, Futures in loops) only after a benchmark, on a pool you sized, with explicit concurrency bounds.
rules.why: A Future starts when built: building them in a loop launches every call at once. .par hands work to a shared pool and slows everything else using it.
rules.how: Throttled traverse (parTraverseN, mapAsync(n)), a Semaphore, or a dedicated ExecutionContext sized from measurement.

patterns.note: Parallel collection; check a benchmark justifies it.
Futures built in a loop: unbounded concurrency.

verify.how: Benchmark shows the gain; the number of tasks in flight is bounded by configuration.
